[Goblin Lore:
Goblins are Primitive humanoids thought to be the result of dark magic, mutation or rape via humanoid bestials with mortals, Goblins are the smallest and and most weakest of the Orc species/Greenskin race yet despite their small stature and fragile frame, Goblins are notorious for being the most intelligent of their race, having comparable intelligence to that of a human. Like all members of the Orc Species/Greenskin race, Goblins are known for their sadistic, vicious tenancies as well as their monstrous like cunning they often display. Despite the danger they often pose, especially in large numbers, due to their weak stature and frame, most warriors, especially those inexperienced, often disregard Goblins as a threat. More often than not, these individuals write these creatures off as pests, citing that due to how weak a Goblin is individually, they can be disregarded as threats. With this type of mindset, many warriors and adventurers often lose their lives or worse, are captured and bred as livestock, with women becoming brood mothers and men become food sources. As goblins often fight in overwhelming numbers, Goblins should never be underestimated, especially when their led by a particularly powerful and/or intelligent individual. Though Goblin horde invasions are quite rare, they should nonetheless be taken seriously as any other horde invasion.

As for their way of life, Goblins typically live in tribes or warbands comprising of other orc species. They are typically led by a Goblin shaman, a warlord or some other powerful or intelligent individual that managed to take power and unlike other orc like societies, Goblin exclusive tribes tend to be a bit more peaceful and at times, even have a working economy of sorts. Being intelligent and able to adapt to situations, Goblins can be capable hunters, ranchers, carpenters and even metal workers though due to their tribes often being nomadic in nature or in locations where rare materials can be difficult to come by, their products tend to be of lower quality, akin to crude iron weapons and tools. Despite their intelligence however, due to their Callous like nature, Goblins prefer to raid and steal from the vulnerable and weak to sustain themselves rather than work the lands themselves. The only known exception to this is the capturing of mortals. Due to being an all male species of orc, Goblins will go out of their way to capture mortals, especially females in the hopes of breeding them to replenishing their numbers. In this instance, despite common misconception, Goblins, for those whom become ranchers, are usually gentle and caring towards those they capture. as these individuals hope to create a viable population of mortal stock that can be used not only for breeding(for themselves and breeding their stock to increase their numbers) but as a food source as well. Though rare, It is not unheard of for goblin ranchers to take pride in breeding a specific bloodline of mortal stock. Such mortals bred from Goblins however tend to have a short and stocky yet sturdy like build though it isn't possible for mortals to retain their ancestor's build through extreme selective breeding. These mortals almost always descend from a goblin stock bloodline however. Half breeds are also known to be born this way though depending on the many circumstances that surround their birth, they are typically rare. For these individuals, they are usually devoured at birth, seen as abominations, or used as mortal stock, though in rare instances, they may be treated as a member of the tribe or be immediately casted out. It all depends on the tribe. No matter who is chosen, within the span of one to two months, their captives or breeding stock will give birth to a litter of several Goblins. It takes six months for a Goblin to reach maturity and for the majority of it, a Goblin requires the milk of their mother. Returning to subject of tribes, in an attempt to hide themselves from the many dangers of the world, Goblins often live in secluded locations like cave or ruins and as such, they have acquired excellent night vision.

As for those whom find themselves within warbands, Goblins often find themselves at the bottom, often functioning as cannon fodder for the stronger of their species as well as the primary labor force, If any at all exists. As warbands are often too focused on raiding and capturing, most warbands have no need for craftsmen or laborers. For those in mixed tribes however, Goblins tend to find themselves in similar positions they would find themselves If they were in a Goblin Tribe. They will often become the tribe's craftsmen and laborers though depending on the nature of the tribe and who leads it, they may not be ranchers or be forced to share that role with other species of Greenskin that can be found in the tribe, notably intelligent orc's whom take a similar liking to that occupation as Goblins do. Nevertheless, due to their weak and at times, cowardly like behavior, unless they can prove themselves useful, Goblins tend to find themselves at the bottom of that tribe's society.]

[Goblin Adventurer

Sometimes referred to titles such as "Hero", "Outcast" or even "Traitor" by other Goblins, Goblin Adventurers are Goblins whom abandoned their old tribal life in favor of exploring the world in the hopes of one day of becoming strong enough, fast enough, and intelligence enough to lead their own tribe(s) or warband. As such, with the exception of the Goblin Paladin and potentially, the Goblin Warlord, Goblin Adventurers are some of the most skilled Goblins in existence, boosting a significantly higher intelligence, physique and a more nimble body than the average Goblin and much like Hobgoblins, Goblin Adventurers tend to be donned in the best armor and weapons they can steal, pillage and in rare instances, purchase. As travelers whom seek to increase their martial strength and knowledge in all things that can assist them in their goals, Goblin Adventurers are similar in nature to a Goblin Paladin, albeit to a lesser extent, being able to learn & adapt to civilized life. By becoming civilized and being able to speak in civilized tongue, a Goblin Adventurer has the opportunity to learn in ways a normal Goblin could never. There is even the possibility a Goblin Adventurer can alter their ideals and set morals though as one might expect, this is rare. It is because of these possible opportunities that a Goblin Adventurer are usually the most skilled and intelligent of their race. That said, much like the Goblin Paladin, they are never a welcoming sight to those of the uncivilized races and depending on the nature and circumstances of the Goblin Adventurer in question, they may or may not be tolerated as a intelligent Bestial or Bestial Kin.]

[Goblin Berserkers

Typically larger in size than the average Goblin, these veteran Goblins have undergone a crude ritual involving the digestion of a number of drugs that, when combined with the ritual performed by a Goblin Shaman, throw the Goblin Warriors into a blood frenzied trance for a substantial amount of time, sometimes permanent, transforming the warrior into a blood thirsty warrior, showing little remorse or care for those around them. Driven nearly insane by their rage to kill, Goblin Berserkers dedicate their purpose to destroying whatever enemy stand before them, usually in the most brutal and barbaric way possible, even at the cost of their own lives. As such, when Goblin Berserkers come upon the enemy, they will waste no time in throwing themselves at the enemy, eager to spill blood in close combat.]

[Goblin Paladin

Without a doubt the most most rarest of the Goblin race, a Goblin Paladin is often a Goblin Adventurer or Warlord who has forsaken their former life in pursuit of serving a Divine for power and influence. As a result, Goblin Paladins are amongst the strongest and most skilled of the Goblin race, usually having no equals besides that of another Goblin Paladin. Depending on the Divine they serve, this may or may not make them the only variant of Goblin that is not outright hostile towards the civilized races. In fact, compared to their lesser brethen, even Goblin Warlords, Goblin Paladins tend to be highly civilized and intelligent, similar to those found in the civilized kingdoms. While a Goblin Paladin is usually never a welcoming sight, they are more often than not, tolerated as much as an intelligent Bestial or Bestial Kin.]

[Goblin Skirmisher

Lightly armored Goblins, these Goblin Warriors specialize in guerilla and skirmishing tactic's, often using their small size and knowledge of their surroundings to confuse and outmaneuver the enemy. Due to their more defensive like tactic's, Goblin Skirmisher are often the defenders of Goblin tribes and camps.]

[Goblin Rider

A rare variant of the Goblin Warrior, these Goblin Warriors specialize in mounted combat through the use of wild or domesticated animals, usually wolves but not always. Being amongst the fastest and more often than not, the most elite within a tribe, Goblin Riders often act as the shock troopers to any Goblin force, using their speed and high agility to confuse, distract and encircle the enemy. Despite their efficiently in skirmishing tactic's, due to their lack of strength and durability, Goblin Riders are often classified as shock troopers and not as light cavalry by the civilized races.]

[Goblin Shaman

Often the elder like leaders of a Goblin tribe or warband but not always, Goblin Shamans are notorious for their ability to employ magic as well as their proficiency in alchemy and rituals, often using their skills to make alchemic goods such as poisons and using crude, painful rituals to enhance their fellow Goblins. Besides for their skill in magic and alchemy, Goblin Shamans are also known for their intelligence, often being the smartest of their race with little exception, that being Goblin Warlords, Adventurers and Paladins.]

[Goblin Warlord

Stronger, faster and far more intelligent than the average Goblin, Goblin Warlords are the greatest of their species with little exception, often being viewed as the undisputed rulers of their race. As their name implies, due to the vast amount of strength and intelligence they wield, these Goblins have climbed their way to the very top of Goblin society, having slaughtered and outwitted their rivals. As such, Goblin Warlords, being the leader of their own warband or tribe(s), have accumulated vast amounts of hordes and resources under their command. Despite this however, they are still a Goblin at their core and as a result of this, Goblin Warlords do not lead from the front, but use their overwhelmingly powerful charisma to sway those under him to fight for him. That being said, having at one point been a Goblin Adventurer themselves, Goblin Warlords are highly skilled in combat and proficient in tactics for a Goblin. As such, a Goblin Warlord should never be underestimated, even by those of significant highly skill.]

[Hobgoblin

Considered a rare breed of Goblin, Hobgoblins are the bigger, stronger, faster cousins of the normal Goblin. Boosting a far more muscular frame as well as a higher intelligence for battle, Hobgoblins are considered the professional, elite soldiers of a Goblin Tribe or Warband, If they are luckily enough to have them. Like Goblin Berserkers, being of a more violent and to a extent, a militant mindset, Hobgoblins have a near unquenchable thirst for fighting. As a result, when not performing their duties as guards or as shock troops, Hobgoblin continually train to improve their skills as well as pillage and loot for better equipment. It's not a uncommon sight for more experienced Hobgoblins to be donned in full armor and wielding weapons that can be found in the civilized lands. Due to their training and combat experience, Hobgoblins tend to be well skilled in close range and long range fighting though the employment of magic seems to be a rarity amongst their race. It is unknown whether or not it's due to their ill aptitude for magic or just preference for wishing to fight with a physical weapon.]
